condition: Fournier’s gangrene (necrotising soft-tissue infection of the perineum)
summary: 61-year-old man with diabetes: 3 days of perineal and scrotal pain and swelling, crepitus, dusky skin, T 38.9, HR 118, BP 94/60, glucose 24, WBC 24, Na 131, creatinine 160, CRP 280. Must not miss: resuscitation, broad-spectrum IV antibiotics and emergency radical debridement.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Severe pain and swelling between the legs
inputs.hpi: Three days of pain in the perineum and scrotum, initially thought to be a boil near the anus. Now rapidly spreading swelling and redness onto the scrotum with dark patches, pain far worse than it looks, fevers and rigors, feels faint. Type 2 diabetes, poorly controlled; drinks heavily.

exam.general: Toxic, confused at times. Temperature 38.9°C, HR 118, BP 94/60, RR 26. Pain out of proportion.
exam.skin: Perineum and scrotum: tense oedema, spreading erythema with dusky necrotic patches, crepitus on palpation, foul-smelling discharge near the anus.
exam.other: Perianal: small discharging abscess at 7 o’clock; necrotic skin extending to the scrotum.

inputs.socialHistory: Fisherman. Drinks 40 units a week. Smoker.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Fournier’s gangrene
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Fournier’s gangrene (necrotising fasciitis of the perineum and scrotum) from a perianal source, with septic shock. Resuscitation, broad-spectrum IV antibiotics, emergency radical debridement.

recommended.note: LRINEC supports but must not delay or exclude the diagnosis (WSES 2018).
recommended.knownGapNote: No LRINEC calculator or CDS rule on web (Wagner and AUDIT are suggested instead).

guideline.name: WSES/SIS-E consensus — management of skin and soft-tissue infections (incl. necrotising soft-tissue infection, Fournier’s gangrene)
guideline.section: Necrotising soft-tissue infection/Fournier’s gangrene: early aggressive surgical debridement, broad-spectrum antibiotics, resuscitation; LRINEC should not be used to rule out
guideline.citation: Sartelli M, Guirao X, Hardcastle TC, et al. 2018 WSES/SIS-E consensus conference: recommendations for the management of skin and soft-tissue infections. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:58.

guideline.name: LRINEC score (Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis)
guideline.section: LRINEC items: CRP, WBC, Hb, Na, creatinine, glucose
guideline.citation: Wong CH, Khin LW, Heng KS, Tan KC, Low CO. The LRINEC score: a tool for distinguishing necrotizing fasciitis from other soft tissue infections. Crit Care Med. 2004;32:1535–1541.

rationale: Base must-not-miss case. The ICD N49.3 (Fournier gangrene) is what the surgeon picks. LRINEC here: CRP ≥ 150 (4) + WBC 15–25 (1) + Hb 11–13.5 (1) + Na < 135 (2) + creatinine > 141 (2) + glucose > 10 (1) = 11 (not asserted as a value; no calculator exists).
